title: County of Pallars Jussà
capsule: Pallars Jussà (lower Pallars) was a Pyrenean Catalan county occupying the lower Noguera Pallaresa valley, separated from Pallars Sobirà by partition in the mid-10th century and centered on Tremp. The county was held by the Pallars dynasty and came under sustained pressure from the expanding County of Barcelona; Ramon IV of Pallars Jussà (d. 1098) was the last significant independent count, and under his successors the county was progressively subordinated. Alfonso II of Aragon formally annexed it in 1192 following the extinction of the comital line, incorporating it into the Crown of Aragon.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's Pyrenean territory is reconstructable from Carolingian and comital diplomas, though the internal division between Pallars Jussà and Sobirà fluctuated and precise boundaries are approximate.
